title: RBAC v2 Launch Checklist (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
body:
Doc purpose
- This is the cross-functional “do not ship without” checklist for RBAC v2 enforcement.
- Audience: Security Eng, Control Plane, Console, SRE, Support Ops, GRC.
- Scope: control plane + console + admin/support tooling + audit log enrichment + Private policy bundle distribution. (Not including data-plane token-level auth beyond tenant/project scoping.)

Definitions / release modes
- Shadow mode / dual-eval: Evaluate RBAC v1 + RBAC v2; do not block based on v2, but emit “shadow-deny” metrics/logs.
- Enforced mode: v2 is authoritative for allow/deny.
- Flags (names vary by service):
  - rbacV2.dualEvalEnabled
  - rbacV2.enforcementEnabled
  - rbacV2.consoleEnforcementEnabled
  - rbacV2.breakGlassEnabled
  - rbacV2.policyBundlePin (for Private)

Owners for launch sign-off (initials)
- Security exec owner: Marcus Lin (ML)
- Release/migration lead: Connor O’Brien (CO)
- Control plane authz: Kaitlyn Nguyen (KN) / Ethan Park (EP)
- Console backend: Chloe Martin (CM)
- SRE incident workflows: Sean Gallagher (SG)
- Audit log enrichment/export: Kevin Osei (KO)
- GRC evidence mapping: Olga Petrov (OP)
- Docs enablement: Elliot Price (EPr) / Kira Thompson (KT)

0) Launch criteria (hard gates)
[ ] Permission inventory coverage: No known P0 endpoints in-scope without an RBAC v2 check (or approved exception with compensating controls).
[ ] Conformance tests in CI enabled (new endpoints must declare permission + check wired). (See pr_18633)
[ ] Audit logs include authz decision context for in-scope services (actor + role_ids + policy_version + decision + reason_code). (See pr_18522)
[ ] Break-glass path is time-bounded, explicitly audited, and alerting is live. (See pr_18560)
[ ] Rollback plan tested in staging and documented (how to disable enforcement / revert policy bundle).
[ ] Support playbook updated: how to diagnose 403s, how to request temporary elevated access, escalation path.

1) Monitoring & dashboards (must exist before enforcement)
Metrics to confirm in each environment (staging + prod)
[ ] Authz evaluation latency (p50/p95/p99) by service and by callsite.
[ ] Policy cache hit rate and cache invalidations (per-org) trending stable. (See pr_18477)
[ ] Shadow-deny rate by endpoint/action (top N) and by customer tier.
[ ] Deny rate after enforcement (watch for step function vs baseline).
[ ] 403 reason_code distribution (unknown_action / missing_scope / not_member / role_missing / policy_parse_error / internal_error).
[ ] Error budget signal: request failures attributable to authz (explicit metric and/or log-based).

Dashboards (links to be filled in by owners)
- Control plane: “RBAC v2 Authz Health”
  [ ] Includes eval latency, cache hit rate, error rate, top shadow-denies.
- Console backend: “Console RBAC v2 Health”
  [ ] 403s by route; correlation with UI releases.
- Audit log exporter: “Audit Export RBAC Fields Adoption”
  [ ] % events carrying policy_version/decision fields; exporter failures.

Log fields (structured logging requirements)
[ ] All authz decisions log: org_id, project_id (if applicable), actor_id, actor_type, role_ids, action, resource, scope, decision, reason_code, policy_version, request_id/trace_id.
[ ] Denies log at INFO with sampling strategy if volume is high; internal errors at ERROR.
[ ] “Policy parse/validation errors” are distinct from “deny” (so dashboards don’t hide real breakages).

2) Alerting (page vs ticket)
Paging alerts (SRE on-call)
[ ] Spike in authz internal errors (policy parse/eval failures) above threshold for 5m.
[ ] Control plane p95 authz eval latency above threshold for 10m.
[ ] Sustained 403 rate increase on critical admin flows (billing updates, SSO config, key rotation) above baseline.
[ ] Policy cache invalidation storm (invalidate rate anomaly) indicating bug/stale assignments.

Ticket alerts (Security/Platform triage)
[ ] Top new shadow-deny actions in Hosted for 24h window (daily digest during rollout).
[ ] Break-glass used (each event creates ticket + Slack notification to #eng-security + #eng-sre).
[ ] Role assignment changes by Support/Impersonation role (audit review queue).

3) Runbook readiness
Primary runbooks to confirm updated and discoverable
[ ] “RBAC v2 rollout + rollback runbook” (includes exact flags, where to toggle, blast radius)
[ ] “403 troubleshooting for Support/CS” (includes reason_code mapping to likely causes)
[ ] “Break-glass usage + approvals + monitoring” (time-bounded elevated session steps)
[ ] “Private policy bundle update + verification” (including signature verification and rollback)

Operational dry-runs (required)
[ ] Staging: simulate policy bundle bad push; verify system fails safe (deny with policy error?) and alert fires.
[ ] Staging: simulate stale role assignment; verify invalidation works and metrics show recovery.
[ ] Staging: simulate break-glass session; verify audit events + alert + expiry.

4) Known risky permissions (must be explicitly reviewed)
Note: list is intentionally short; these are the “most damaging if mis-scoped” actions.

Support / impersonation
[ ] support.impersonate_user (if enabled) restricted to Support/Impersonation role; requires ticket id; time-bounded.
[ ] support.read_customer_secrets is NOT allowed by default (explicit deny / no role includes it).

Org / identity
[ ] org.update_sso_settings restricted to Org Admin + Security Admin only (not Developer).
[ ] org.manage_roles / org.assign_roles requires separation-of-duties review (cannot be granted to Billing Admin by default).

Keys and access
[ ] api_keys.create / rotate / revoke restricted; ensure Read-only cannot list secrets.
[ ] service_tokens.create restricted; verify least privilege for automation accounts.

Billing and commercial
[ ] billing.update_payment_method restricted to Billing Admin / Org Admin.
[ ] billing.view_invoices allowed to Billing Admin + Org Admin; ensure Security Admin is view-only unless explicitly granted (per CISO request in reviews).

Dedicated / infra controls
[ ] dedicated.update_autoscaling_policy restricted to Dedicated Admin / Org Admin; ensure Developer cannot mutate GPU pool config.
[ ] dedicated.gpu_pool.modify is P0; requires explicit role and audit log.

Audit logs / export
[ ] audit.export is treated as sensitive (P0/P1 depending on data fields); default: Security Admin + Org Admin only.
[ ] Ensure export destination configuration changes are audited and permissioned separately (audit.export_config.update).

Policy administration
[ ] rbac.policy.update (Hosted internal only) restricted to platform admins; with change review and signed bundles for Private.

5) Comms plan (internal + customer-facing)
Internal comms
[ ] Launch announcement draft posted to #eng-platform, #eng-security, #support, #cs-enterprise with:
  - what is changing (403 reason codes, role UI, support workflow)
  - expected increase in “deny” logs during enforcement
  - how to escalate if a customer is blocked
[ ] Create “RBAC v2 rollout war room” Slack channel for rollout window (time-bound).
[ ] Support macros updated: “RBAC v2 permission denied” response template and required info to collect (org_id, request_id, action, time).

Customer comms (by tier)
Hosted
[ ] Status page/internal release note: “Stronger role-based access controls” (no scary language; emphasize least privilege)
[ ] If customer has custom SSO group mapping: send heads-up + link to role mapping guidance.

Dedicated
[ ] CSM brief: any endpoints that changed behavior (autoscaling policy, GPU pool config). Include workaround path if needed.
[ ] Identify top 20 Dedicated customers by admin activity; proactive check during shadow phase.

Private
[ ] Private upgrade notes include:
  - policy bundle version included
  - how to pin policy bundle version
  - offline/air-gapped update steps
  - signature verification steps and failure behavior
[ ] Customer enablement doc: role matrix + “common enterprise roles” examples.

6) Rollout plan checklist (execution)
Pre-rollout (T-7 to T-2 days)
[ ] Dual-eval enabled in prod for at least 7 days for Hosted control plane + console backend.
[ ] Shadow-deny triage: top offenders reviewed; fixes merged or documented exceptions created.
[ ] Confirm no “unknown_action” denies in shadow mode for common flows (indicates missing permission annotations).
[ ] Policy bundle v0.1 validated and pinned; schema validation is enforced in CI.

Rollout day (T0)
[ ] Change window confirmed; on-call coverage confirmed (Platform + SRE + Security).
[ ] Enable enforcement for a canary cohort first (by org allowlist or % rollout), monitor for 60–120 minutes.
[ ] Expand to 25% / 50% / 100% with explicit go/no-go gates.
[ ] Track key user journeys:
  - create key / rotate key / revoke key
  - update billing payment method
  - update SSO/SAML config
  - update Dedicated autoscaling policy
  - view/export audit logs

Rollback readiness (must be possible in <10 minutes)
[ ] Clear instructions for disabling enforcement without redeploy.
[ ] Clear instructions for reverting policy bundle version (Hosted) and pinning/rolling back in Private.
[ ] Confirm dashboards show recovery after rollback (deny rate normalizes).

7) Post-launch tasks (T+1 to T+30)
24 hours after 100% enforcement
[ ] Review deny logs for: “should have been allowed” vs “correct deny” buckets.
[ ] Create follow-up tickets for missing role documentation, confusing reason codes, UX gaps.
[ ] Verify audit log exporter compatibility (no customer SIEM ingestion breakage reported).

Weekly for 4 weeks
[ ] Access review: list of orgs with newly created high-privilege roles/assignments.
[ ] Break-glass review: any use must have ticket + approval + after-action note.
[ ] Review top 10 most-used sensitive actions; confirm least-privilege roles still match reality.

Governance
[ ] Confirm “new endpoint must declare permission” CI check is enabled for all relevant repos and not bypassed.
[ ] Establish monthly RBAC change review (Security + Platform + GRC):
  - new permissions added
  - role matrix changes
  - policy bundle version bumps

8) Evidence & audit readiness (SOC 2 / customer security reviews)
Evidence artifacts to generate and store
[ ] Screenshot/export of role matrix (default roles) and separation-of-duties statement.
[ ] Example audit log events showing authz decision context (allow + deny) with fields present.
[ ] Record of rollout approvals (change management ticket or release note with sign-off).
[ ] Break-glass policy and sample event trail (redacted) showing time-bounded access.

GRC notes
- OP to confirm which artifacts map to which SOC 2 controls and where they are stored for audit (GRC tracker link TBD).

Appendix A: “Stop the line” conditions
Immediately rollback / pause rollout if any of the following occur:
- P0 admin flow blocked for multiple customers (billing, SSO config, key rotation) with confirmed RBAC mis-scope.
- Authz internal error rate suggests policy parsing/eval instability.
- Break-glass used repeatedly as workaround (indicates systemic permissioning issue).
- Audit log exporter failures that prevent customers from receiving audit data (for customers with contractual obligations).

Appendix B: Quick triage checklist for 403s
Collect:
- org_id, actor_id, actor_type
- request_id/trace_id
- endpoint + action/resource/scope
- reason_code
- policy_version
Then check:
- Is the actor in the org/project?
- Are the role assignments correct and propagated (cache invalidation)?
- Is the action name missing/renamed in policy bundle?
- Is this a console-only flow calling a backend route without updated enforcement flag?

Changelog
- 2025-03-14 (ML): Marked final for Hosted enforcement ramp; added explicit “audit.export restricted to Security Admin/Org Admin” note after review.
- 2025-03-10 (CO): Added canary ramp gates + stop-the-line conditions.
- 2025-02-25 (KO): Added audit log exporter verification items + required fields list.
